17. In the application dated 4-2-92 before the Returning Officer no objection was raised regarding those double seals but the fact remains that no objection regarding casting of false votes or putting double seals in the ballot papers were raised nor any prayer was made before the Presiding Officer for recounting. In the instant case the Election Tribunal itself could not say and was not in a position to say whether the double marks were put during election or the acts of some interested persons afterwards. In such a position their Lordships of the Appellate Division, on the similar facts, have held in the case reported in 38 DLR (AD) 275, 276 that; "When the Tribunal itself was not in a position to say whether the double marks were post-election acts or were the doings of the respective voters, election of the returned candidate should not have been interfered with. It is not a case of benefit of going to a defeated candidate feeling aggrieved like the accused in a criminal case. Here, presumption is in favour of the returned candidate, whose election shall not be declared a nullity unless the Tribunal "is satisfied" as laid down in Rule 49, that the election has been materially affected by some illegal acts or contravention of some Rules. "In this particular case opposite party petitioner was declared elected and challenging the declaration applicant opposite-party No. 1 filed Election Tribunal Case No. 8 of 1992 which was dismissed and against that an appeal was preferred being Election Tribunal Appeal No. 4 of 1992. The learned Appellate Tribunal after hearing assessed the evidence on record in its entirety and felt it necessary for ends of justice that the recounting should be made with respect to the two centres namely; Waruk High School Centre and Dopolla Janata High School Centre and sent back the case on remand to the Tribunal. Accordingly, the tribunal after re-counting again declared the opposite party petitioner as the successful candidate. As against this judgment and order Tribunal Appeal No. 6 of 1993 was preferred. On perusal of the impugned judgment and order it appears that the case was sent back on remand to the Tribunal only for recounting the ballot papers of 2 centres named aforesaid, the learned appellate tribunal committed an illegality in reopening the whole case and assessing the evidence again in its entirety and passed the impugned judgment and order contradicting his earlier findings totally ignoring the dispute in question. On careful consideration of the evidence and the impugned judgment and order, it appears that the learned Appellate Tribunal on conjecture found that though the applicant secured 112 votes more than the opposite party petitioner the Presiding Officers in collusion with Assistant Presiding Officer by putting double seals on 187 ballot papers declared the opposite party petitioner elected and that the Election Tribunal by his judgment and order dated 31-05-93 also illegally declared him elected. This finding appears to me is based on no evidence on record and as such, his decision cannot be sustained in law. 

 18. Admittedly no written prayer was filed before the Presiding Officer for recounting of the ballot papers on any allegation of malpractice and admittedly the tribunal did not find that the election has been materially affected by any corrupt practice or violation of any Election Rule, the appellate tribunal committed an illegality in not at all considering these legal aspects of the matters. Furthermore, the tribunal itself when was not in a position to say whether the double marks on ballot papers were post-election acts or were the subsequent doings of the respective voters, the election of the petitioner cannot be interfered with. In such a position the presumption is always in favour of the returned candidate which cannot be declared a nullity unless the tribunal "is satisfied" as laid down in Rule 49, that election has been materially affected by some illegal acts or contravention of some Rules. In view of the principles laid down by their Lordships in the aforesaid decision reported in 38 DLR (AD) 275, 276, exactly on the similar facts, the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned appellate tribunal is liable to be set aside.
